name: Volcanic & aviation ash
value: No red aviation codes found (13 Nov)
summary: No red aviation codes, VEI 4+ eruptions or ash airspace closures found as of 13 Nov; Mayon stays at Alert Level 3
state: Searches on 13 Nov found no red aviation colour code, no VEI 4+ eruption and no major ash-related airspace closure. Mayon in the Philippines remains at Alert Level 3 after a moderately explosive eruption on 30 Oct; a minor eruption on 3 Nov sent ash 1,600 m high and about 3,900 people had evacuated, with no flight disruption reported (Daily Tribune). That is a local hazard rather than one affecting major air routes, so the signal stays Normal.
for_you: Air travellers face no significant ash disruption. Residents near Mayon should follow Phivolcs and local authorities, including the 6 km permanent danger zone.
rubric_hit: Normal: no aviation colour code red and no large eruption found; Mayon at Alert Level 3 is a local hazard

sources.title: Daily Tribune — Mayon spews ash plume, displaces nearly 4K residents

why: Major eruptions ground flights (Iceland 2010) and can cool the climate for years.
drivers: Volcanic unrest; impact depends on ash plume height and jet-stream direction.

rubric.alert: Major airspace closures from ash, or a VEI 4+ eruption.
rubric.watch: Aviation colour code orange/red at a volcano near major air routes, or a large eruption.
rubric.normal: No aviation colour code red; no large eruptions.
